title: Pange lingua, st. 1
source: Pange lingua gloriosi corporis mysterium (St Thomas Aquinas)
text:
Pange, lingua, gloriosi Corporis mysterium, Sanguinisque pretiosi,
Quem in mundi pretium Fructus ventris generosi Rex effudit gentium.
notes:
English: Sing, my tongue, the Saviour's glory, / Of His Flesh the mystery sing; / Of the Blood, all price exceeding, / Shed by our immortal King, / Destined, for the world's redemption, / From a noble womb to spring.

Latin: Pange lingua gloriosi corporis mysterium, St Thomas Aquinas; the received text of the Roman Missal. English: Edward Caswall's translation (Lyra Catholica, 1849) as printed in Matthew Britt, The Hymns of the Breviary and Missal (1922), pp. 183-185, archive.org/details/hymnsofbreviarym00britrich. Both public domain.

title: Pange lingua, st. 2
source: Pange lingua gloriosi corporis mysterium (St Thomas Aquinas)
text: Nobis datus, nobis natus Ex intacta Virgine, Et in mundo conversatus, Sparso verbi semine, Sui moras incolatus Miro clausit ordine.
notes:
English: Of a pure and spotless Virgin / Born for us on earth below, / He, as Man, with man conversing, / Stayed, the seeds of truth to sow; / Then He closed in solemn order / Wondrously His life of woe.

Latin: Pange lingua gloriosi corporis mysterium, St Thomas Aquinas; the received text of the Roman Missal. English: Edward Caswall's translation (Lyra Catholica, 1849) as printed in Matthew Britt, The Hymns of the Breviary and Missal (1922), pp. 183-185, archive.org/details/hymnsofbreviarym00britrich. title: Pange lingua, st. 3
source: Pange lingua gloriosi corporis mysterium (St Thomas Aquinas)
text: In supremae nocte cenae Recumbens cum fratribus, Observata lege plene Cibis in legalibus, Cibum turbae duodenae Se dat suis manibus.
notes:
English: On the night of that Last Supper / Seated with His chosen band, / He, the Paschal victim eating, / First fulfills the Law's command: / Then as Food to all His brethren / Gives Himself with His own hand.

Latin: Pange lingua gloriosi corporis mysterium, St Thomas Aquinas; the received text of the Roman Missal. English: Edward Caswall's translation (Lyra Catholica, 1849) as printed in Matthew Britt, The Hymns of the Breviary and Missal (1922), pp. 183-185, archive.org/details/hymnsofbreviarym00britrich. title: Pange lingua, st. 4
source: Pange lingua gloriosi corporis mysterium (St Thomas Aquinas)
text:
Verbum caro, panem verum Verbo carnem efficit:
Fitque sanguis Christi merum,
Et si sensus deficit, Ad firmandum cor sincerum Sola fides sufficit.
notes:
English: Word made Flesh, the bread of nature / By His word to Flesh He turns; / Wine into His Blood He changes: / What though sense no change discerns? / Only be the heart in earnest, / Faith her lesson quickly learns.

Latin: Pange lingua gloriosi corporis mysterium, St Thomas Aquinas; the received text of the Roman Missal. English: Edward Caswall's translation (Lyra Catholica, 1849) as printed in Matthew Britt, The Hymns of the Breviary and Missal (1922), pp. 183-185, archive.org/details/hymnsofbreviarym00britrich. title: Pange lingua, st. 5
source: Pange lingua gloriosi corporis mysterium (St Thomas Aquinas)
text:
Tantum ergo Sacramentum Veneremur cernui:
Et antiquum documentum Novo cedat ritui:
Praestet fides supplementum Sensuum defectui.
notes:
English: Down in adoration falling, / Lo! the sacred Host we hail; / Lo! o'er ancient forms departing, / Newer rites of grace prevail; / Faith for all defects supplying, / Where the feeble senses fail.

Latin: Pange lingua gloriosi corporis mysterium, St Thomas Aquinas; the received text of the Roman Missal. title: Pange lingua, st. 6
source: Pange lingua gloriosi corporis mysterium (St Thomas Aquinas)
text:
Genitori, Genitoque Laus et iubilatio, Salus, honor, virtus quoque Sit et benedictio:
Procedenti ab utroque Compar sit laudatio. Amen.
notes:
English: To the everlasting Father, / And the Son who reigns on high, / With the Holy Ghost proceeding / Forth from Each eternally, / Be salvation, honor, blessing, / Might, and endless majesty.

Latin: Pange lingua gloriosi corporis mysterium, St Thomas Aquinas; the received text of the Roman Missal. English: Edward Caswall's translation (Lyra Catholica, 1849) as printed in Matthew Britt, The Hymns of the Breviary and Missal (1922), pp. 183-185, archive.org/details/hymnsofbreviarym00britrich. Both public domain.
